messages:
Erin (CS): Pasting a short customer-facing runbook for go-live: main focus = graceful prefill, tiny batching for interactivity, stream fallback, and renewal-signal capture. Will attach snippets.
Marco (SE): Can you include a one-line explanation of why soft prefill vs hard prefill for customers? helps with their engineers.
Erin (CS): sure: soft_progressive prefill ramps requests over first 20-40s to avoid GPU spikes while still reducing cold latency.
Sana (Eng): eng notes: default batch_window_ms=30, max_batch_tokens=180. KV cache common-prefix TTL=600s. recommend warm-pool of 1-3 nodes for small accounts first 48h.
Erin (CS): client config to share:
```json
{"prefill":true,"prefill_mode":"soft_progressive","prefill_seconds":30,"batch_window_ms":30,"max_batch_tokens":180,"stream":true,"client_keepalive_s":20}
```
Vik (PM): include rollout safety: run a 10-prompt eval 24h after go-live and whenever model variant changes. if >2 failures -> route to stable.
Marco (SE): troubleshooting snippet for streams (pasteable):
```bash
# check SSE endpoint
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/check?model=prod-1
# grep for x-request-id in service logs
rg "x-request-id" /var/log/redwood/*
```
Jess (CS): survey plan: 48h post-live short pulse (accuracy Likert, latency ok Y/N, any hallucinations Y/N). negative answers auto-tag renewal_risk and schedule CS follow-up.
Sana (Eng): fallback policy: on eval regressions >3 in 1h, switch routing to higher-fidelity variant for 10min, alert oncall, and increase prefill jitter to spread load.
Ops-bot: Reminder: warm-pool prewarm will run for onboarding-tagged accounts at 05:00 UTC tomorrow.
Erin (CS): adding a tiny traffic profile example for SREs:
```json
{"peak_qps":10,"avg_tokens":50,"interactive":true,"session_seconds":100}
```
Marco (SE): Ill include the one-pager in the kickoff email template. thanks Erin.
Erin (CS): perfect. I'll publish this as "Onboard Pocket Runbook" in the playbook folder and set a 20m sync for CS+SE next week to walk through. Closing thread. /end
